claim: A model-proposed, gate-verified computer-use loop now runs against a real browser in this repository, and a taught trajectory replays with zero model calls.

what_is_new.function: act(goal) -- propose, gate, execute, causal_check, verify, or REFUSE
what_is_new.memory: record_trajectory / replay, keyed on the starting screen hash

the_number_that_matters.definition: fraction of trajectories that replay without a model and still verify
the_number_that_matters.honest_scope: two toy pages; not a benchmark

bugs_found_by_running_it_not_by_reading_.detail: PIL raised OSError on a truncated PNG outside the import guard; the loop died instead of failing closed. The hostile test found it.
Focusing a text field moves ~0.16% of the frame; the 2% floor refused a correct click. r53's mistake in a new domain.
Typing 11 characters moved ~1900 px = 0.9% of the claimed band. Fixed by using absolute changed pixels for 'did something happen here' and a fraction for 'did it happen elsewhere'.
focus ring 1896 px vs heading swap 3250 px, a factor of 1.7. Any global pixel threshold here is theatre; a 'none' claim was made checkable only as a claim about a PLACE.
An earlier demo had already pressed the button; clicking again changed nothing and the gate refused correctly while the test blamed the loop.

what_this_does_not_prove: It is not a benchmark result. Two five-element pages are not OSWorld.
The verifier is still a model reading a screenshot. The gate bounds it; it does not replace it.
Replay is keyed to the exact starting screen hash; any layout or content change forces the model path.
No desktop applications: no display server and no window manager on this machine. Browser only.
Planning across pages is not built. Each act() run has one goal on one screen.
